Notes: Listed on an early Watch The Throne tracklist given out by music insider blog The DOTR. Fully finished with a hook and verse from Ye, alongside a JAŸ-Z verse later reused on "Fuckwitmeyouknowigotit" from his album Magna Carta... Holy Grail. According to Aziz Ansari, "We were sitting there, and we were watching some basketball game or something... Jay Z’s just kind of staring off, and he just taps Kanye, and he very quickly whispers this rap, It was one of the raps in the song and he had just come up with it, and it was long and so complicated". Samples "Por Ti Volare" by Andrea Bocelli, which could not be cleared, being the reason it was cut. The beat was originally given to Lil B for his song "New York Subway", and was later brought to Watch The Throne sessions by Karlyle. One of the holy grails of unreleased Ye tracks. LQ snippet leaked May 2019. Three more LQ snippets of Kanye's verse leaked before it leaked in full LQ on November 13th, 2023. Lossless snippets leaked on September 21st, 2026. While the groupbuy for the song finished on September 24th, 2026, issues pertaining to the transfer of funds by the holder lead to the leaking of the song being delayed to November.

This particular version features an extended intro with fully finished vocals from both Ye and James Blake, originally not known about until Ye would play it amongst other WAR files on a stream May 1st, 2025. In this intro, Ye mentions the idea of turning into birds after death, alluding to how Ye and Kim shared the belief that their deceased parents would visit them in spirit as crows, as mentioned in the 500 Days in UCLA documentary and in Ye's "Bad People" freestyle. Has two equally long Ye verses and a short Ye bridge that is repeated many times throughout the song, initially thought to be James Blake. Track 9 on the October 2022 copy. Would eventually be released on BULLY with the intro and James Blake cut, finished Ye vocals, and different production. Original snippet leaked on Christmas Eve 2025. On Christmas Day 2025, a $10,000 groupbuy would open and finish in less than 24 hours, with the song leaking shortly thereafter.

OG Filename: VALEE X YE X LIL PUMP I LOVE IT (UPDATED)
In September 2018, a source claimed that the original version featured Valee instead of Lil Pump. Valee's manager, Andrew Barber, confirmed this version existed in November 2018, but called it a remix, however it's been confirmed by sources to be an OG. According to a trusted source, Valee was removed from the song because "Lil Pump didn't want one of Kanye's artists on the track". Lil Pump would reuse his verse from this version for his song "Be Like Me".

OG Filename: Off The Grid - 07.18.20 Evan Kit
Pusha T reference track, with different production from E.VAX. Was the version played by Kanye with Playboi Carti and Rick Rubin, during the Mercedes Benz sessions in 2021 from the infamous "Alright, play Off The Grid" meme, shown in both the leaked mini Donda documentary and the In Whose Name? documentary. Kanye said he didn't want to use the verse, Carti then asked why, and Kanye responded that it was because he didn't want no "Black Lives Matter shit" on the album, and said that Black Lives Matter was "worse than the devil" and called it "mind control", due to Pusha's heavy mention of Black Lives Matter and police brutality in his verse.

OG Filename: trav uzi pressure
Former holy grail of the Ye community. This version has Travis Scott doing the bridge and harmonizing over the "Get Off Me" interlude along with the "clear search history" line cut. Originally thought to have been from Turbo Grafx 16, though this version at the very least is from SWISH sessions. Short recording of Che Pope playing the song over Instagram Live surfaced on October 23rd, 2020. The main melody is sampled from "Haunted" from the Maniac Soundtrack. Also contains a minute long intro sample from the 2012 film Silver Linings Playbook. Stem bounce leaked after Luit sold the song in a $25k groupbuy, which finished in just under 9 hours with the support of multiple unreleased communities providing bonuses and donations. Later released on VULTURES 2 DIGITAL DELUXE 5 with vocals from Ty Dolla $ign and a punch-in on the line "You the type of nigga shop at Uniqlo, just found out my father-in-law unisex", following the popularity of the leak.

OG Filename: POOTIE TANG TP ANT BONGO SCOTT
Solo Ant Clemons version. According to xtcy, the file was in a folder of Jeremih and Ant Clemons tracks. According to Ant Clemons in a Rolling Stone article, "the first day [Bongo ByTheWay and I] met we did 11 records". The article later states "Bongo stayed awake for long enough to be impressed with Clemons’ output. He took Clemons to meet Jeremih; West called on Jeremih to come to Wyoming to participate in the sessions for Ye, Jeremih played West a demo with Clemons titled 'All Mine' and West pounced on it". According to Ant Clemons, the song was shown to Ye one week before the album's release. ROBOTSCOTT's release credit likely comes out of courtesy for him being a large contributor to this version of the song and shaping the vision, as none of this production is on release and the stems do not mention him at all. Snippet of what looks to be a scrapped music video posted by Legion on Instagram February 10th, 2018.

Notes:

Release ready version of the song. Almost identical to the SNL 40 version, but now with Frank Ocean on the intro and different production on Sia's verse, as well as one less line on her verse compared to previous versions. Meant for the now scrapped A Side / B Side single release of "All Day" & "Wolves", which was meant to release on February 24th, 2015 based on Ye's iTunes Artist Page updating, Joe Perez's single art, MIKE DEAN hyping it up on Twitter and Benji B being confused by it's delay on Twitter. Was delayed by a week for unknown reasons and the next release day of March 3rd, 2015, "All Day" released on it's own without "Wolves". (prod. Kanye West)
(Never See Me Again)
Notes: Unfinished track, with some mumble lyrics, leaked from just over a month before My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy dropped. Rumored to be recorded early 2010 for Winter Spring Summer Fall. Was leaked as "Never See Me Again", but current leakers who have the song confirm that the title is "See Me Again". Interpolates "I Never Want To See You Again" by Quasi. This leak gained notable popularity after a widespread theory that it was a "suicide note" of sorts, further influenced by the discovery that the song shared a similar chord progression to "Futari Dake No CEREMONY" by the late J-pop star Yukiko Okada, who comitted suicide in April of 1986 due to alleged relationship issues - which can allude to Kanye's troubles at this time that would result in his breakup with Amber Rose - however this relation has since been debunked and is mostly viewed as a coincidence.
